# dlarfg

> Generates a real elementary reflector H of order N, such that.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlarfg from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlarfg';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlarfg( N, alpha, x, strideX, tau ) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the reflector |
| `alpha` | `Float64Array` | in/out |  |  | scalar, overwritten with beta on exit |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `1 + (N - 2) * abs( incx )` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | `x` stride length |
| `tau` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output scalar |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the elementary reflector.
- `alpha`: On entry, the value $\alpha$. On exit, it is overwritten with the value $\beta$.
- `x`: On entry, the vector x. On exit, it is overwritten with the vector v.
- `tau`: The value $\tau$.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `x`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlarfg.ndarray( N, alpha, offsetAlpha, x, strideX, offsetX, tau, offsetTau ) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the reflector |
| `alpha` | `Float64Array` | in/out |  |  | scalar, overwritten with beta on exit |
| ↳ `offsetAlpha` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index into alpha array |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `1 + (N - 2) * abs( incx )` |  | vector, overwritten with v on exit |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for x |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for x |
| `tau` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output scalar |
| ↳ `offsetTau` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index into tau array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the elementary reflector.
- `alpha`: On entry, the value $\alpha$. On exit, it is overwritten with the value $\beta$.
- `x`: On entry, the vector x. On exit, it is overwritten with the vector v.
- `tau`: The value $\tau$.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `x`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

## Notes

-   `dlarfg()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARFG`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlarfg.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlarfg from './../lib/base.js';

// Generate a Householder reflector for a 4-element vector [3; 4; 0; 0]:
const alpha = new Float64Array( [ 3.0 ] );
const x = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 0.0, 0.0 ] );
const tau = new Float64Array( 1 );

dlarfg( 4, alpha, 0, x, 1, 0, tau, 0 );

console.log( 'beta (alpha on exit):', alpha[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => beta (alpha on exit): -5

console.log( 'tau:', tau[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => tau: 1.6

console.log( 'v:', x ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => v: Float64Array [ -0.8, 0, 0 ]
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARFG`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLARFG generates a real elementary reflector H of order n, such that

$$
H \, \begin{pmatrix} \alpha \\ x \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} \beta \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} , H^T \, H = I
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars, and x is an (n-1)-element real vector. H is represented in the form

$$
H = I - \tau \, \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ v \end{pmatrix} \, ( 1 v^T )
$$

where $\tau$ is a real scalar and v is a real (n-1)-element vector.

If the elements of x are all zero, then $\tau = 0$ and H is taken to be the unit matrix.

Otherwise $1 \le \tau \le 2$.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
